GitHub is an online software development platform that provides a secure environment for developers to store, collaborate on, and manage their code projects through Git version control. It was founded in 2008 by Thomas Legend, Pavel Domenchuk, Max Kuhn, and Chris Sorenson as part of Linus Torvalds's open-source project called Bitbucket. Today, GitHub is a global community of more than 14 million developers that includes millions of users worldwide.

GitHub offers various features for collaboration on projects, including:

- A browser-based code editor (WebIDE) allowing real-time editing and viewing
- Version control using Git
- Secure repositories to host your project's source files
- Continuous integration tools to help automate testing
- A built-in issue tracker with labels, fields, milestones, etc.
- Public or private access options for projects
- Multiple programming languages supported (Python, JavaScript, Java, C#, Go, Ruby)

GitHub is a go-to platform for collaborative software development and has been instrumental in the rise of open-source projects. It provides free services that range from basic Git hosting to advanced features like automatic bug tracking, continuous integration, and integrated feature requests.

As of 2021, GitHub had over 30 million active users globally, making it one of the most popular websites for software development collaboration.
